result.summary: Agenor sends his son Cadmus to find his sister Europa, who has been carried off by Jupiter, and forbids him to return without her. Cadmus consults Phœbus's oracle, follows a heifer to the spot where she lies down, and prepares a sacrifice. Nearby, a dragon sacred to Mars lurks in a cave.

scenes.title: Cadmus exiled and seeks oracle
scenes.summary: Agenor orders Cadmus to find Europa or stay in exile. After wandering the world, Cadmus asks Phœbus's oracle where to settle.
scenes.stakes: Cadmus risks permanent exile from his homeland and his father's wrath if he cannot find Europa.

scenes.title: The oracle's command
scenes.summary: Phœbus tells Cadmus to follow an unyoked heifer and found a city where she lies down.
scenes.stakes: Cadmus needs a home, having no place to return to.

scenes.title: Following the heifer
scenes.summary: Cadmus follows the heifer past the Cephisus and Panope until she lies down. He gives thanks and sends servants for water for a sacrifice to Jupiter.

scenes.title: The dragon's grove
scenes.summary: The ancient grove hides a cave with a spring and a poisonous, triple-tongued dragon sacred to Mars.
scenes.stakes: The servants sent for water are about to face a deadly guardian.

notable_quotes.reason: Wry remark that no one can uncover Jupiter's intrigues, excusing Cadmus's failure.

analysis.text: Cadmus's exile follows from a god's whim, showing human fates shaped by divine desire and the injustice of Agenor's harsh command.
The oracle and the heifer begin a foundation myth, linking wandering and divine guidance to the founding of Thebes.

legacy.text: The story of Cadmus founding Thebes by following a cow was a popular foundation myth, retold by later writers and artists.

fun_facts.text: Ovid's Metamorphoses opens Book 3 mid-story, continuing Jupiter's abduction of Europa from the end of Book 2.

language_notes.text: Phœnicia was the coastal homeland of Agenor and Cadmus, roughly modern Lebanon; Cadmus is barred from returning without Europa.
"Affectionate and unnatural": Agenor's love for his daughter is shown by the search, but banishing his son if he fails is cruel.
The rhetorical question hints that Jupiter (the Greek Zeus) was the true culprit, so Cadmus's exile is unjust.
The Castalian cave is by the Castalian spring at Delphi, Apollo's oracle site, sacred to Phœbus and the Muses.
"Reverberate" means to echo; the heifer's lowing fills the air.
A libation is liquid poured out as an offering to a god; here water is needed for the sacrifice.
Mars (the Greek Ares) was god of war; a dragon sacred to him foreshadows violence, since killing it will bring consequences.

context_notes.text: Phœbus is Apollo, god of prophecy, whose oracle at Delphi was consulted before founding colonies.
The Cephisus is a river in Phocis and Bœotia; Panope was a town in Phocis, so the route runs toward Bœotia.
A grove untouched by the axe was typically sacred, so entering it risks offending a deity.

literary_notes.text: Cadmus's silent adoration and patient following show him as pious and obedient to divine guidance.
The hidden dragon, introduced just after the servants are sent for water, signals the danger awaiting them.
Fire, poison and triple rows of teeth build a vivid, frightening picture of the beast.
